description.p: Skykeep brings your iCloud notes, reminders, calendar, contacts, Drive and photos to your computer as fast desktop apps. Your library is kept on this machine, so everything opens straight away, even offline, and what you change here reaches your iPhone and your other devices.

Sign in once with your Apple Account. Your password stays on this computer, in your system keyring. Skykeep connects to Apple for your iCloud, and to the calendars you subscribe to and the calendar accounts you add yourself; the AppImage also checks GitHub for new versions of Skykeep. There is no Skykeep account and no analytics.

Skykeep is an independent, open-source project. It is not made by, endorsed by, or affiliated with Apple, and it reaches iCloud through interfaces Apple has not published, so Apple may change them at any time.

screenshot.caption: Skykeep, with your six apps and your account

description.p: Photos no longer downloads Apple's screen-sized picture of every photo to draw the grid: it is drawn from Apple's thumbnails, as Photos does, so a large library takes a few gigabytes once instead of tens of gigabytes again and again. Videos whose first frame is black are no longer downloaded just to look for a better picture.

On Linux, the iCloud Drive folder mounts again when files written before a restart were still waiting to be sent, and sends them. Update and Restart no longer waits forever on a change iCloud refused; refused changes stay for you to send again or let go.

In Reminders, the tag field suggests the tags you already use as you type, most used first. Chinese, Japanese and Korean names read family name first, as Apple's Contacts shows them, in Contacts and in Calendar's birthdays. Folders whose names begin with a dot, like an Obsidian vault's .obsidian, now sync from Windows and Linux, so settings, plugins and themes reach your other devices.

A new reminder keeps its due date and flag even when Apple turns that step away for a moment: the change waits and is sent again, and subtasks moved or deleted with their reminder go the same way. After an answer from Apple it couldn't read, sign-in now waits before trying again instead of starting over on every sync. Every answer from iCloud is read within a size limit, and a connection that drops part way through is retried as a dropped connection.

Skykeep now reads in French, thanks to turbotiste. When Apple's iCloud session lapses, Skykeep renews it by itself instead of stopping with an error: on Android, iCloud Drive and syncing no longer stay stuck until you sign out and in again. In Settings, your account's name and storage stay readable on a narrow window.

Skykeep now reads in Bahasa Indonesia, thanks to x-edwart. A backup no longer moves apps and other packages from iCloud Drive into Earlier versions and fetches them again on every pass, thanks to szuszupaks. In Photos, choosing Newest First or Oldest First opens on the newest photos at once instead of showing old ones first. In Whole photos only the photo itself counts: a selection can start in the space beside a photo and takes a photo only once it reaches it. Dragging a selection with Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) now selects and deselects photos, and with Shift adds them. Settings shows where Skykeep is made, on GitHub.

Large uploads to iCloud Drive and Photos no longer stop after a minute, and one cut short by a dropped connection is sent again by itself. Photo and video downloads are checked to the last byte and carry on where they stopped. In File Explorer, photos and videos open while they download, iCloud Drive files open on slow connections, a folder cut short while listing is listed again, names with accents show as typed, and when the disk runs low, iCloud files you haven't used recently are freed (pinned and open files stay). A backup to a network drive that isn't mounted now waits for it instead of filling your disk. On Android, pictures and PDFs in notes show and open. A duplicated photo with one copy edited shows each copy as it is, Photos' sort menu says where the newest photos are, and clicking the tray icon closes the window when it's in front.
Photos opens on your newest photos at once in a large library, in either sort order: it no longer loads your oldest months first, and scrolling while a view loads keeps you among the newest photos.
Photos now opens straight on your newest photos even in a very large library, instead of showing your oldest photos for a moment first and then moving.

Other programs can now use Skykeep. Launchers, status bars and scripts can add reminders, events and notes with the skykeep command, and read today's reminders, upcoming events, notes and contacts as JSON in a fraction of a second, without opening a window. See docs/cli.md. Notes, Reminders and Contacts now reopen on the list, folder and item you left them on. Title bars follow the appearance chosen in Settings. Typing in a long note is faster. In Windows' iCloud Drive folder, an editor that saves every few seconds, such as Obsidian, no longer leaves conflicted copies of your notes. On Linux, Move to Trash in the Drive folder no longer makes a hidden .Trash folder in iCloud Drive. Skykeep now stays signed in when Apple sends a one-off unexpected answer or an empty list of services, and when iCloud asks it to wait it waits as long as asked. An interrupted backup no longer stops later backups, quitting during a window resize no longer hangs, and the Drive and Photos folders stay mounted through an error Skykeep recovers from. Skykeep also checks iCloud less often for apps whose windows aren't in front.

Photos now opens on your newest photos at the bottom every time, and stays there when you make the window bigger, full screen or smaller again. Before, it could open at your oldest photos or land in the middle of the library depending on the window's size. Scrolled up to older photos, resizing the window keeps the same photos in view, and a jump to a month lands exactly on it.

On Linux, Skykeep no longer stays invisible at start when the system keyring is locked and its unlock prompt doesn't appear: after a minute it opens and says the keyring is locked. In the Snap, Open at Login now starts Skykeep, and the Drive and Photos folders, which the Snap can't provide, are no longer offered. Where the system's fusermount3 is missing, the Drive folder now says to install fuse3 instead of showing an unexplained error.

Photos opens as it does on a Mac and an iPhone: oldest at the top, newest at the bottom, and on your newest photos. Newest First is still in the sort menu, and a sort you chose before is kept. A month of thousands of photos, such as a large Screenshots library, shows at once instead of a blank block. Clicking a year now opens Months on that year, where on some Linux setups it landed a few rows away, and switching to Months no longer downloads pictures it doesn't show. Drive's window updates when you open it or come back to it, instead of waiting up to five minutes.

On Windows, files deeper than 260 characters in the Drive folder now sync, where they stayed "Sync pending", and a Drive folder placed on an exFAT or FAT drive or a network share says why it can't work there. On Linux, a fault in one request can no longer disconnect the Drive folder, and the Fedora package (COPR) builds again. Changes waiting to upload are kept safely through a power cut, a sign-in the system keyring wouldn't save is always said, and each sync writes less: records that didn't change aren't saved again, and Calendar isn't read whole every five minutes.

Opening an app no longer freezes Skykeep on Windows, a problem that came with 0.1.27; on Linux the same freeze could catch an app opened while Skykeep was already running, and it is gone too. A window closed the moment it opens now stays closed. On Linux, closed app windows give their memory back: before, each one kept its web process, about 100 MB, until Skykeep quit. Photos keeps every picture on screen in a large library, where tiles could turn into grey boxes a few seconds after opening or after dragging the scrollbar. A download kept from an earlier update no longer installs over a newer version. On Windows, the Drive folder shows as on while it comes back after a restart rather than off, a folder File Explorer refuses one item in still opens with the rest, and folders opened before a restart are kept up to date again.

On Windows, an app's window opened again at the size it was left, Reminders at its smallest for example, no longer freezes Skykeep or stays white. Each app's window can float on top of others: the pin beside the sidebar button, or Ctrl+Shift+P (Windows and X11). Reminders shows pinned lists in the order they were pinned, as the iPhone does. Notes' Sort Checked Items is in Settings as Apple has it, Manually or Automatically. The words still in English in the German and Chinese apps are translated. New on Linux, as a beta: an iPhone over the cable as this computer's camera and microphone, in any app, from Settings, iPhone.

Settings has a new layout: a sidebar of sections beside one section at a time, with Home first: your account, its storage, Sync Now and Sign Out, then the six apps. Switches no longer flip when Settings opens. Calendar starts the week on the right day from the first moment when the system's date format and language differ, instead of redrawing it a moment later.

On Windows, the Drive folder in File Explorer comes back on by itself after a restart, and folders open instead of failing with "The cloud operation is invalid"; if the folder can't start, Settings says why. Photos sorted Oldest First opens at the newest photos. Every app now comes in Simplified Chinese and German, with dates in the chosen language, and Reminders lists show the icon chosen on the iPhone, emoji included. The Keyboard Shortcuts sheet is easier to read. On Linux, each app's icon shows in every launcher and dock. On Android, three home-screen widgets: Reminders, Quick Reminder and Agenda.

Custom smart lists made in Reminders show their reminders again: a list of tags matching any of them showed empty, and Skykeep now reads every rule Reminders offers, from tags and lists to include or leave out to each Date and Time choice. Other programs can tick a reminder off, put it back or open it in Reminders from the command line. On Linux, docks show the main window with its icon when Skykeep is installed from the .deb or .rpm.

On Windows, each app opens from its tile in Skykeep's window again. Calendar shows the events of every calendar, including those unticked in the Calendar on icloud.com, which Skykeep listed but left empty. Skykeep's window, Settings, sign-in and all of Notes now come in German and Simplified Chinese, with a language picker in Settings. The button that shows and hides each app's sidebar now matches the rest of the toolbar.

Notes keeps what you typed when you quit, close its window or sign out. Two Apple Accounts on one computer never mix: reminder and event alerts, the Hidden album's lock, calendar subscriptions and unfinished downloads stay with their own account, and signing in as someone else starts clean. Favorite, Hide and Delete in Photos are kept safely until iCloud has them, even if Skykeep closes first. Lists open faster with large libraries, each app's window loads only its own app, and typing with an input method no longer acts on half-typed words. Skykeep has its own colours and sign-in, an Open-Source Licences window in Settings, and an updated SQLite with a security fix.

Saving over a file in the iCloud Drive folder keeps it the same file in iCloud, so apps on your other devices that follow it, such as a password manager's database or a document left open, still have it, and its earlier versions stay in iCloud. Notes can put a link on the words you select, with Ctrl+K or from the Aa menu, and offers a link you have just copied. Open at Login waits for the tray before keeping the window closed. When iCloud is busy, an app's tile says so in a few words, and Calendar asks again on its own when a connection stalls.

Every app's window has a sidebar button, at its top left or with F9, that hides the sidebar and brings it back, remembered for each app. Calendar can add Nextcloud and other CalDAV calendars beside iCloud's, with Nextcloud signing you in on its own page. A small Calendar window brings your calendars over the month from its More menu, a small Drive window its places from the sidebar button, an event's popover stays on screen as it grows, Keyboard Shortcuts shows the app in front and is never cut off, and Send to iPhone has its own icon. A reminder set for a time with no time zone shows and rings at that time wherever you are.

Skykeep now opens to a launcher of your six apps, each showing what it holds and how fresh it is; Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Drive and Photos each open in their own window, and Settings fit on one calm page. Downloading large iCloud Drive folders no longer crashes Skykeep, notes save cleanly every time, and every sidebar moves with the arrow keys.

Send files to your iPhone from your file manager's right-click menu, back up every photo and everything in iCloud Drive to a folder or drive you choose, and see iCloud files' thumbnails in File Explorer. Each app now has its own icon. Photos upload several at once, files go into notes again, and Reminders syncs even when an alarm holds a date no calendar has.

Skykeep stays signed in and never sends a code to your iPhone on its own, works with Advanced Data Protection, downloads whole iCloud Drive folders, keeps both edits when an event changes on two devices, and stays fast with very large photo libraries.

Skykeep starts on every Windows PC with nothing else to install, says why when it can't pick up your session or Apple asks you to wait, saves your sign-in reliably while Windows Defender checks the file, and leaves updates to Scoop when Scoop installed it.
When Apple doesn't accept a password, Skykeep now says so plainly, and that an app-specific password can't sign in.

Every Apple ID signs in, an AppImage for Ubuntu 22.04 and newer, a locked Hidden album in Photos, Keep Both or Replace when pasting in iCloud Drive, drag and drop inside windows on Windows, and fixes across every app.
The first release of Skykeep: iCloud Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, iCloud Drive and Photos as six desktop apps with one sign-in, kept on your computer and in sync with your iPhone.

ul.li: Notes and Reminders changes from your iPhone usually arrive in about a second
Everything opens instantly and works offline, and your edits sync when you reconnect
A note edited here and on your phone at the same time is merged, not overwritten
Search across every app, quick capture, and reminder alerts with Complete and Snooze
